observations.body: Joseph and Asenath’s two sons receive names through which Joseph speaks about toil, his father’s house, and fruitfulness in affliction.
observations.label: Manasseh and Ephraim are named before the famine

payload.posture: Read Genesis 41:50–52 as one movement in Joseph's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states joseph and Asenath’s two sons receive names through which Joseph speaks about toil, his father’s house, and fruitfulness in affliction. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Joseph's story.
payload.title: Manasseh and Ephraim are named before the famine
